look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check the alternate twice-pinnate (sometimes nearly thrice-pinnate) leaves with toothed leaflets, then the hanging clusters of round yellow drupes. In flower, inspect the conspicuous dark staminal tube at the center.
taxonomy_notes: Accepted Melia azedarach L. in Kew POWO. Do not confuse with Sapindus saponaria (western soapberry), Pistacia chinensis or Ailanthus altissima.

project_inclusion.source_pool: Master Plant Pool row 702 / installer preflight
project_inclusion.notes: POWO documents native range in Asia to northern/eastern Australia, not Texas. Introduced/exotic encounter taxon. No unsupported invasive label or fabricated county PASS/FAIL.

morphology_keys.habit: Deciduous small to medium tree, often with a spreading crown and hanging fruit clusters.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Alternate, twice-pinnate to nearly thrice-pinnate compound leaves; individual leaflets have conspicuously toothed margins.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Loose clusters of small five-petaled pale lilac flowers; dark purple staminal tube is a strong structural cue.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Round fleshy drupes that mature yellow and can persist after leaves fall; photograph cluster attachment and fruit close-up.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Inspect alternate leaf attachment and twigs; leaf scars and buds need diagnostic close-ups.

confused_with: Sapindus saponaria (western soapberry): generally once-pinnate leaves with mostly untoothed leaflets; compare fruit and leaf architecture.
Pistacia chinensis (Chinese pistache): once-pinnate leaves and small drupes in clusters, but not the large bipinnate toothed leaves of chinaberry.
Ailanthus altissima (tree-of-heaven): large once-pinnate leaves with basal leaflet teeth/glands; fruit are winged samaras, not round drupes.
comparisons.key_distinctions: Large alternate bipinnate leaves with toothed leaflets, lilac flowers with a staminal tube, and persistent yellow drupes.
